passages.context: Corpus Thomisticum paragraph [87761], chapter 3 lectio 6 on Galatians 3:15-18, was inspected in full with the adjacent lectiones. Aquinas treats the divine promises as a firm testament: Abraham is the one for whom they are to be fulfilled and his Seed the one through whom they are fulfilled. He identifies the singular Seed as Christ, the only one through whom and in whom all can be blessed, and argues that the Law given later cannot void the promise or make the inheritance arise from Law rather than promise.
passages.notes: The Corpus Thomisticum controller uses paragraph [87761]. The registered claim is Aquinas's Christological and promissory reading of Galatians 3:15-18. It does not by itself establish the historical-linguistic range of the Hebrew collective noun in Genesis.

passages.context: Corpus Thomisticum paragraph [87762], chapter 3 lectio 7 on Galatians 3:19-20, was inspected in full with lectiones 6 and 8. Aquinas orders the Old Law to four purposes: repressing malice, manifesting human weakness, taming concupiscence, and instructing ignorance by figures of future grace. He says it stood in an ordered place until Christ, the promised Seed. He permits either Moses and Aaron as God's messengers or angelic ministry in 'ordained by angels.' In 'the hand of a mediator' he names Christ Lord of the Law and the Law in Christ's power, while Moses, in whose hand it was given, signifies Christ. He then gives three expositions of the mediator: Christ is true God and man; he is not mediator of Jews alone but sufficient to reconcile all; and he mediates not one people only but Jews and Gentiles, the Son being mediator while God remains one.
passages.notes: The claim is bounded to Aquinas's own fourfold account and his several stated readings of Galatians 3:19-20. Aquinas expressly treats the increase of transgression after the written Law as sequential, not as the Law's causal production of sin. The passage neither denies Moses's historical ministry nor warrants collapsing other patristic readings of the mediator into Aquinas's synthesis.

passages.context: Corpus Thomisticum paragraph [87763], chapter 3 lectio 8, was inspected in full; the reusable passage bound here is its opening exposition of Galatians 3:21-22. Aquinas answers 'God forbid': the holy Law is not contrary to God's promises. It cannot confer the life of grace and eternal beatitude or justify in place of faith, but it serves the promised grace by making sin and human impotence known and thereby moving a person to seek Christ. He reads the promise as grace given through faith in Jesus Christ not only to Jews but to all believers.
passages.notes: Lectio 8 continues through Galatians 3:25. Its exposition of custody under the Law and the Law as pedagogue belongs to verses 23-25 and lies outside this registered Galatians 3:21-22 claim bound. The record therefore does not license presenting that later pedagogical exposition as wording on the narrower liturgical pericope.
